messages.author: 46f7d5745f0539b0
messages.subject: General question about occupancy models
parts:
Hello unmarked folk,

I am new to occupancy modeling. I have a data set to analyze but unfortunately the protocol is biased: they chose all their transects because they knew that the bird of interest was present.

- my 1st question is how biased is the probability of detection if I run an occupancy model anyway? I mean, let's say I have a p=0.73 in habitat 1 and a p= 0.59 in habitat2 even if I can't rely on the absolute value of p returned by the model, could I still trust the relative results (i.e. here detection is higher in habitat 1).

- They surveyed 13 sites 10 times and each survey is a transect with 5 points. The observation points of this study are 200m apart, so I was thinking in using the data as replicated counts to get information on the detection probability. Again, I was wondering to what extent results would be reliable? Would probability of detection (and abundance) results be reliable for the 13 sites surveyed?

I'm sorry, my questions are probably very trivial, but I'm just trying to get at least some useful information from that data set.

Have a great WE,
Chloé

messages.author: 00ebeb6e0521112d
messages.subject: RE: [unmarked] General question about occupancy models
parts:
Dear Chloe,

that's no problem at all that you have if you're only interested in detection probability, except that if you really KNOW that all sites are occupied, then you should simply fit a logistic regression. You can do this with glm() or, if you want to account for non-independence of measurements at the same site, use glmer() with a site random effect.

If you're only interested in detection, then you're actually in a better position when you don't have to also estimate occupancy.

Best regards  --- Marc

messages.subject: Re: [unmarked] General question about occupancy models

Dear Marc,

Thank you a lot for your answer!
So that's cool for the detection probability, that's what we've done this morning, except I've just calculated the relative frequency of detection, and then ran the glm on it.
Thanks for pointing out the non-independance of data (I forgot to account for it).

I might be interested in getting the abundance though. If I use a pcount model on the dataset, would the abundance (inferred only for the 13 sites of the study of course) be influenced by that Bias in the protocol? (they want to re-do the protocol on the exact same 13 sites for the non-reproductive period, so I was hopping that instead of change in occupancy, we could at least get the difference in abundance for those selected 13 sites)

Best regards,
Chloé

messages.author: 00ebeb6e0521112d
messages.subject: RE: [unmarked] General question about occupancy models
parts:
Dear Chloe,

if your interested in abundance and if you have counts, then you could fit the binomial N-mixture model or even if you have detection/nondetection, you could try and see whether the Royle/Nichols model gives you sensible answers. However, in that case you would have to accept that your result would be biased by an unknown degree by your non-random site selection. But you might hope that perhaps you just get the intercept of the abundance model too high, but the coefficients with any site covariates might not be biased perhaps ?

Best regards  --- Marc
